statements.action_statement: Use the default ES256 signing algorithm. Only a deployment that opts into RS256 (`[oauth2] signing_algorithm` or an RS256 JWS token key) performs RSA private-key operations and is exposed to the Marvin timing side channel; RSA public-key operations (verification of RS256 DPoP proofs, federation JWKS, JWS) are not affected. No patched `rsa` release exists.

No patched release is reachable yet: crypto-bigint 0.5.5 is pulled in only by jsonwebtoken's rust_crypto backend (p256/ecdsa 0.13), which signs the default ES256 tokens; Keystone's own p256 use is already on the patched 0.14 line. The affected operations run on secret scalars during ES256 signing, but remote exploitation needs per-signature timing measurements and a lattice attack on partially known nonces and is judged impractical; a co-located observer is a stronger threat. Operators should not share the host CPU with untrusted workloads and should rotate signing keys on the normal schedule. The project moves to a patched p256 when jsonwebtoken releases on it, or to jsonwebtoken's aws_lc_rs backend.
